prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Phoenix to fix my air conditioning?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” HVAC company that fits every situation — the right choice depends on your exact location in Phoenix, the problem (repair vs replacement), your budget, any brand warranty requirements, and whether you need emergency service. I can find highly rated local options for you if you tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood, but here’s how to pick the best company and some things to look for:

What I recommend you do
- Give your ZIP code or neighborhood so I can pull top-rated companies near you.
- Decide whether you want a quick repair now or a replacement/major work that can be scheduled.
- Ask for at least 2–3 written estimates for comparison.

Must-have qualifications and checks
- Arizona license: verify the contractor’s Arizona Registrar of Contractors (ROC) license number on the ROC website.
- EPA 608 certification: required for handling refrigerants.
- Insurance: ask for proof of liability insurance and workers’ comp.
- NATE certification (North American Technician Excellence) is a good indicator of trained technicians.
- Warranty: ask what’s covered (parts/labor) and for how long.

Where to research and reviews
- Local Google and Yelp reviews for recent customer experiences.
- Better Business Bureau (BBB) for complaints and ratings.
- Angi/HomeAdvisor for vetted pros and job histories.
- Social/local Facebook groups can give quick first-hand referrals.

Questions to ask any company before hiring
- Are you licensed and insured? What’s your ROC license number?
- Are your technicians EPA-certified and NATE-certified?
- What’s the diagnostic fee? Is it applied to the repair cost?
- Can you provide references or recent reviews?
- Do you offer a written estimate and a parts/labor warranty?
- How long will the repair take and do you offer emergency/same-day service?

Red flags
- No ROC license or refusal to provide it.
- Pressure to replace when a repair might suffice (get a second opinion).
- Very low initial price but vague or no written warranty.
- Poor or no online presence/reviews.

Typical costs and expectations (very rough)
- Diagnostic fee: commonly $75–$150.
- Minor repairs (capacitor/contactor/thermal switch): often $100–$500.
- Major repairs (compressor, coil): $500–$2,500+ depending on parts and labor.
- Full system replacement: several thousand dollars depending on system size and efficiency.

If you want, tell me:
- Your ZIP code or neighborhood in Phoenix
- Brief description of the problem (no cool air, short cycling, strange noises, leaking, etc.)
I’ll find top-rated local HVAC companies, compare reviews, note specializations (repairs vs replacements), and point out any currently advertised deals or emergency options.
